entry.text: The Psalmist had in the former verse directed the young man to diligence and attention unto the word; but the word doth nothing unless we join prayer; and therefore now he gives an example in his own person.
entry.insight: Manton moving from verse 9 to verse 10 of Psalm 119: attention to the Word is commanded, and then David immediately prays. Scripture and prayer are not two devotions but two halves of one conversation.

entry.text: This prayer is a standing monument of Christ's affection to the church; it did not pass away with the external sound, or as soon as Christ ascended into heaven, and sat at the right hand of the Father; it retaineth a perpetual efficacy; the virtue remaineth, though the words be over.
entry.insight: Manton on the high-priestly prayer as a copy of Christ's continual intercession. Like the word of creation, the prayer keeps its force as if newly spoken; the Son is still praying his people home.

entry.text: Out of the whole, learn to see Christ in the word, to use Christ in prayer; he is the golden pipe by which our prayers ascend, and the influences of heaven are conveyed to us.
entry.insight: Manton's summary of Christ's mediation: he speaks to us in the word and for us in prayer. Nothing goes up and nothing comes down except through him; the comforts of providence and conscience have their one channel.
